is_anopheles.evidence: Study evaluated Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected as larvae in M'Bé, Côte d'Ivoire (Page 3, 'Mosquito collections and maintenance').

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w), Vgsc L1014S (kdr-e), and Ace-1 G119S (ace-1R) (Page 3 & Page 5, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Reports genotype counts and allele frequencies for N=226 mosquitoes: for L1014F in M-form, 16 RR, 114 RS, and 93 SS (frequency 0.33); for L1014S and Ace-1 G119S, 0% frequency (Page 5, Table 2).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquito larvae collected in May 2012 from rice paddies in M'Bé valley (5.209963° W, 7.970241° N), central Côte d'Ivoire (Page 2 & 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical research paper reporting field collection, WHO bioassays, molecular genotyping, and biochemical assays.

sub_country_location.evidence: M'Bé valley (5.209963° W, 7.970241° N), 30 km north of Bouaké, Bandama department, Côte d'Ivoire (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard primary study reporting specific field collections in May 2012.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts, frequencies, sample sizes, and bioassay results are fully reported within the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance and underlying mechanisms in Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected in May 2012 from M'Bé, Côte d'Ivoire. Genotyping of 226 mosquitoes identified the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) allele at a frequency of 0.33 (16 RR, 114 RS, 93 SS in M-form), while Vgsc L1014S and Ace-1 G119S were absent (0%). WHO tube bioassays with 10 insecticides with/without PBO and biochemical assays were also performed.
